day: # The propers of the Mass (Introit, Lessons, Epistle, Gradual with the
# Alleluia or Tract, Gospel) as the 1962 Missal appoints them under the
# rubrics of 1960: every Sunday, the temporal feasts, the Ember days, every
# weekday of Lent and Passiontide, Holy Week (Ordo of 1955), the Easter and
# Pentecost octaves, Rogation Monday, the Vigil of the Ascension (Rogation
# Wednesday), and the feasts of the I, II and III
# class and the vigils.  From Divinum Officium
# commons in web/www/horas, Tabulae; commit 4b479e10, read October 2026)
# resolved as it does for "Rubrics 1960"; the citation is the one at the head
# of each part.  The Missal's Vulgate (Douay) numbering is given in the
# Hebrew way for the Psalms and for the chapters that break differently
# (tradition.csv verse_numbering); Sirach, Tobit, Esther 10-16 and Daniel 3
# keep the Vulgate's.  Book names are the English ones (1 Samuel for 1 Kings
# Sirach for Ecclesiasticus, Revelation for the Apocalypse).
#   Weekdays outside Lent repeat the Sunday's Mass and are not given (Rogation
#   Tuesday among them: Divinum Officium gives it no propers of its own); a Lenten
#   feria gives way to a I or II class feast, and a III class feast on a
#   Lenten feria or an Advent or September Ember day is titled
#   "Commemoration of ...".  Introit and Gradual citations join their verses
#   in order of the Psalter, not of the chant.
